text.arabic_uthmani: وَتَرَىٰهُمْ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا خَٰشِعِينَ مِنَ ٱلذُّلِّ يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِىٍّۢ ۗ وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ فِى عَذَابٍۢ مُّقِيمٍۢ

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction joining the new vision to the prior judgment scene
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes the prior judgment discourse and carries it into a new visible tableau. The connector lets the ayah shift from the preceding scene in 42:44 into exposure, verdict, and final seal without making the vision feel like a separate anecdote; the same doomed group now appears exposed rather than speaking.

topics.headline: opening link into the exposure tableau
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the exposure scene as continuation from 42:44 rather than as a detached new episode.
topics.reason: The prefixed connector and boundary rows support continuity while allowing a new visual beat.

words.gloss_range: seeing and recognizing, narrowed here to witnessed public disclosure of the object group
words.root_gloss_range: broad seeing, perceiving, and recognizing field; local grammar selects direct witnessing with recognition pressure
words.prose: {{ar:تَرَىٰهُمْ}} ({{tr:tarāhum}}) makes the addressee the witness and makes the exposed group the object before the passive verb explains their display. The sight root carries recognition as well as seeing, so the later speech can interpret what the eye has been made to witness; the contrast with {{ar:يَنظُرُونَ}} ({{tr:yanẓurūna}}) keeps the addressee's clear view opposite their faint looking.

topics.headline: the addressee sees them before the display is explained
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the doomed group is made visible to the addressee before the passive exposure unfolds.
topics.reason: The second-person imperfect with attached object pronoun fixes the watched group first, while later sight language contrasts clear witnessing with their restricted gaze.

words.gloss_range: being presented or displayed, narrowed here to forced passive exposure before the punishment referent
words.root_gloss_range: presentation, display, setting before, and turning-away branches; local passive with complement selects public presentation
words.prose: {{ar:يُعْرَضُونَ}} ({{tr:yuʿraḍūna}}) suppresses the presenter and foregrounds the wrongdoers as patients being displayed. The root range includes presentation and display, and here the passive imperfect makes that exposure ongoing as forced confrontation with the punishment referent; echoes of judgment presentation (18:48; 69:18) sharpen the irony that bodies are fully displayed while only a hidden glance remains.

topics.headline: passive display removes agency and publicizes consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees punishment begin as compelled visibility, not only as later pain.
topics.reason: The Form I passive foregrounds the patients and the complement points the display toward the punishment context; parallels in 18:48 and 69:18 sharpen judgment-display without controlling the local parse.

words.gloss_range: prepositional pronoun complement marking the object before or toward which they are displayed
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهَا}} ({{tr:ʿalayhā}}) completes the exposure vector after the passive verb. Its feminine suffix leaves the referent unnamed, so the reader recovers the Fire or punishment context from the discourse, and the preposition keeps both facing and being brought up against the consequence spatially active.

topics.headline: pronoun-complement points the display toward punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader must recover the unnamed feminine punishment referent, tightening the link with the surrounding judgment context.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is governed by the passive display verb and its feminine suffix depends on the prior punishment scene for reference.

words.gloss_range: humbled or lowered state, narrowed here to visible abasement during exposure
words.root_gloss_range: lowered body, voice, eyes, stillness, and awe; local context turns the field into disgraced bodily reduction
words.prose: {{ar:خَٰشِعِينَ}} ({{tr:khāshiʿīna}}) is not a separate label but the state in which they are seen. The loweredness field makes defeat visible in body, bearing, and force, and this lowered body-state will be matched by the fading glance; the plural participle spreads that settled abasement across the group, while {{ar:ٱلذُّلِّ}} ({{tr:al-dhull}}) names the pressure from which it comes.

topics.headline: loweredness is the state in which they are seen
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees inner defeat made legible as posture before the verdict names their loss.
topics.reason: The accusative participle functions as a circumstantial state of the object pronoun, and the following humiliation phrase specifies the source.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking source or cause for the humbled posture

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: source or channel particle for the gaze

words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) turns the following noun into the source or cause of the lowered state. The first prepositional phrase explains posture from humiliation, while the later {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) channels looking from an edge, so body and vision both arise from constrained origins.

topics.headline: from humiliation explains the humbled state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader does not read humbledness as vague mood; it has a named source in humiliation.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the humiliation noun and attaches to the circumstantial participle, with a later parallel preposition narrowing the gaze.

words.gloss_range: recognized humiliation, disgrace, and subjection as the source of their lowered state
words.root_gloss_range: lowliness, tractability, and subjugation; local phrase selects abasement that removes dignity and agency
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلذُّلِّ}} ({{tr:al-dhull}}) names the abasement as a definite, recognized force. The root field joins disgrace with being made manageable, so the humbled posture is both loss of dignity and loss of agency; links with imposed disgrace (3:112) and divine abasing (3:26) reinforce that judgment texture.

topics.headline: definite humiliation becomes the force-source of abasement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices humiliation as an encompassing condition, not merely a momentary embarrassment.
topics.reason: The definite verbal noun after the source particle abstracts humiliation into the condition producing the visible posture; variant vowel evidence does not alter the local root field.

words.gloss_range: looking, waiting, or considering, narrowed here to ongoing constrained looking under exposure
words.root_gloss_range: looking, attending, considering, and waiting; local phrase selects a restricted gaze with waiting-pressure only as resonance

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: direct witnessing of the exposed group

words.prose: {{ar:يَنظُرُونَ}} ({{tr:yanẓurūna}}) gives the exposed group a remaining action, but it is a diminished one. The root can include looking and waiting; here the ongoing active verb is narrowed by the following edge phrase, reversing {{ar:تَرَىٰهُمْ}} ({{tr:tarāhum}}): the addressee sees clearly while they look only from a restricted margin.

topics.headline: active looking remains, but only as diminished agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a reversal of vision: they are clearly seen, but their own looking is reduced to a furtive channel.
topics.reason: The active imperfect resumes the same exposed group as minimal agents, and the following prepositional phrase restricts the way they look.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the source, channel, or instrument of the gaze

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: source or cause particle for humbled posture

words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) narrows the act of looking by giving it a source or channel. After {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) made posture come from humiliation, this second preposition makes the gaze come from an edge, mapping constraint onto both body and perception.

topics.headline: from an edge narrows the visual channel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the gaze constrained at the preposition before the edge noun even arrives.
topics.reason: The second preposition governs the glance noun and parallels the earlier source phrase for humiliation.

words.gloss_range: edge, eyelid, or glance, narrowed here to a small marginal channel of perception
words.root_gloss_range: edge, extremity, eyelid, and glance imagery; local construction selects restricted visual margin

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: faint hidden quality of the glance

words.prose: {{ar:طَرْفٍ}} ({{tr:ṭarfin}}) turns looking into edge-perception. The root image of edge or eyelid narrows the gaze to a marginal glance, and its indefinite singular form keeps the sight small; with {{ar:خَفِىٍّۢ}} ({{tr:khafiyyin}}), the phrase becomes a mechanism of restricted vision rather than a normal act of looking.

topics.headline: the eye is reduced to a marginal glance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees not ordinary looking but sight squeezed into a single faint edge.
topics.reason: The indefinite singular noun governed by the preposition and modified by the hidden adjective forms a restricted-gaze mechanism; parallels such as 14:43 and 55:56 support constrained glance imagery.

words.gloss_range: hidden or faint, narrowed here to the quality of the marginal glance
words.root_gloss_range: concealment and hiddenness; local adjective agreement makes the concealment a faint visual quality, not successful cover
words.prose: {{ar:خَفِىٍّۢ}} ({{tr:khafiyyin}}) agrees with {{ar:طَرْفٍ}} ({{tr:ṭarfin}}), so the hiddenness belongs to the glance, not to the exposed bodies. The result is local reversal: public display has stripped away concealment, and what remains hidden is only a faint, fading quality in their perception.

topics.headline: hiddenness survives only inside the diminished glance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that hiddenness remains only as a weak quality of gaze while the people themselves are exposed.
topics.reason: The adjective agrees with the glance noun and cannot govern the whole scene; judgment hiddenness parallels such as 20:7 sharpen but do not replace the local grammar.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction pivoting from visual narration to quoted evaluation
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots from the visible tableau into a new speaker frame. It links the quote to what has just been seen, but it also prevents the gaze phrase from collapsing directly into speech, giving interpretation its own beat.

topics.headline: connector opens the believer-speech frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels a turn from seeing the scene to hearing its interpretation.
topics.reason: The prefixed connector opens the speech clause while keeping it linked to the visual narration.

words.gloss_range: saying or declaring, narrowed here to completed public verdict-speech by believers
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, and declaration; local perfect verb selects a completed quoted verdict, not fabricated speech
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) moves the ayah from display to definition. The perfect speech verb presents the believers' statement as a completed verdict, so the visible humiliation is not left uninterpreted; sight is followed by saying, and the desperate question of 42:44 gives way to authoritative evaluation.

topics.headline: speech converts exposure into verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the scene interpreted by authorized speech after it has first been made visible.
topics.reason: The perfect speech verb introduces a quoted clause by the believing subject; contrast with fabricated saying in 69:44 remains a boundary, not the local sense.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun introducing the speaker class completed by the faith clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prior faith identity of the speakers

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) delays the noun-like identity of the speakers into a relative construction completed by {{ar:ءَامَنُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}). That framing matters: the quote is not anonymous commentary, and the later repeated relative pronoun will define the losers by a different criterion.

topics.headline: the speakers are defined before their quote
topics.reader_payoff: The reader knows who is authorized to speak before hearing the definition of loss.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is the subject of the speech verb and its following clause defines the speakers.

words.gloss_range: having believed, narrowed here to prior faith-identity that enables truthful interpretation
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, safety, and faith-commitment; Form IV locally selects believing while retaining trust/security pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) completes the speaker identity with prior faith. The root field of security and trust is narrowed by Form IV into belief-commitment, and that matters because those who believed in the unseen can now name the meaning of what has become visible; the same-surah reward thread in 42:22 stands behind their position.

topics.headline: faith identity authorizes the interpretation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the verdict comes from those whose faith lets them interpret visible judgment correctly.
topics.reason: The Form IV perfect completes the relative clause and is objectless; unseen-belief parallels such as 2:3 support interpretive capacity without changing the local verb.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle governing the quoted nominal definition
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) gives the believers' words the shape of emphatic definition. It governs the loser label and makes the quoted clause answer a scene that could otherwise be read only as spectacle; the later {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) will mirror this emphasis at the closing destination.

topics.headline: emphasis turns the quote into definition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the believers define true loss, not merely comment on it.
topics.reason: The particle governs the first nominal clause in the quote and prepares the mirrored final emphatic clause.

words.gloss_range: losers or those in deficit, narrowed here to the named class whose loss is then defined
words.root_gloss_range: commercial deficit, loss, and forfeiture; local participle becomes an identity label explained by the following verb and objects
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-khāsirīna}}) names the class before the proof is stated. The commercial deficit field of the root is redirected into existential forfeiture: the ayah does not leave loss as bad outcome or failed profit, because the following words define the losers as those who lost themselves and their people.

topics.headline: the loser label is defined by self-and-family forfeiture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees loss recoded from ordinary deficit into losing oneself and one's belonging.
topics.reason: The definite active participle under the emphatic particle is immediately explained by a repeated finite verb; 103:2 and 39:15 support the broader loss field and formula.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun introducing the defining clause for the loser class
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) turns the label into a criterion. After {{ar:ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-khāsirīna}}), the relative clause explains who counts as the losers, and its repetition contrasts with {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}): one relative construction authorizes the speakers, the other defines the doomed class.

topics.headline: relative clause supplies the criterion for the label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader receives a criterion for the label rather than a bare moral category.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun functions as predicate or explication after the definite loser label.

words.gloss_range: they lost or forfeited, narrowed here to completed transitive forfeiture of explicit objects
words.root_gloss_range: loss, deficit, and forfeiture; local transitive perfect selects forfeiture of self and family

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: family or belonging as lost object

words.prose: {{ar:خَسِرُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:khasirū}}) repeats the loss root as a finite verb, making the definition grammatical rather than merely rhetorical. Because it takes {{ar:أَنفُسَهُمْ}} ({{tr:anfusahum}}) and {{ar:أَهْلِيهِمْ}} ({{tr:ahlīhim}}) as objects, the loss is transitive forfeiture: they have lost what should have been most their own.

topics.headline: the repeated loss root becomes transitive forfeiture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the loser label grounded in a completed act whose objects are named.
topics.reason: The perfect verb takes two explicit direct objects and answers the preceding active participle; 7:9 supports self-loss recurrence.

words.gloss_range: selves, persons, or lives with possessive suffix, narrowed here to the primary object of forfeiture
words.root_gloss_range: selfhood, person, life, breath, and precious value; local possessed plural selects their own selves as lost objects
words.prose: {{ar:أَنفُسَهُمْ}} ({{tr:anfusahum}}) is the first object of {{ar:خَسِرُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:khasirū}}), so the definition begins with self-loss. The possessive suffix intensifies the paradox: what is grammatically theirs is precisely what they forfeit, and the root range of self, life, and precious personhood makes the loss more than bodily defeat.

topics.headline: the self is the first forfeited object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the paradox that they lose the very selves marked as theirs.
topics.reason: The noun is the first direct object of the loss verb and carries their possessive suffix; judgment parallels such as 82:19 sharpen the loss of self-control.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle joining the second object to the same loss verb
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the second object under the same loss verb. It expands one forfeiture from inward selfhood to outward belonging, making the self-and-family formula a paired unit rather than a list of separate misfortunes.

topics.headline: coordination expands one loss across two domains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears self-loss and family-loss as one paired forfeiture, not two unrelated losses.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates a second object under the same transitive verb.

words.gloss_range: family, household, people, or belonging circle with possessive suffix, narrowed here to their own belonging forfeited at judgment
words.root_gloss_range: household, people, eligibility, and belonging; local plural/collective object selects family-belonging rather than narrow lineage alone
words.prose: {{ar:أَهْلِيهِمْ}} ({{tr:ahlīhim}}) extends the loss to their household and belonging-circle. The word is broader than a narrow lineage term, and the possessive suffix marks this as their own sphere; in judgment, what might seem protective is itself forfeitable, an inversion sharpened by family-warning and family-exclusion scenes (66:6; 11:46).

topics.headline: family and belonging are forfeited with the self
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that judgment strips not only the isolated self but also the protective circle of belonging.
topics.reason: The noun is the coordinated object of the loss verb and carries their possessive suffix; 66:6 and 11:46 support moral redefinition of family-belonging.

words.gloss_range: day or event-time, narrowed here to the temporal frame of manifest judgment
words.root_gloss_range: day, time, and decisive event; local construct selects eschatological event-time rather than ordinary daylight

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: Day of Standing as judgment time

words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) places the self-and-family forfeiture at decisive event-time. It is not ordinary daylight here; as an accusative temporal adverb in construct, it waits for {{ar:ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ}} ({{tr:al-qiyāmah}}) to specify the Day on which loss becomes manifest and no longer negotiable.

topics.headline: the day marks when the loss becomes manifest
topics.reader_payoff: The reader locates the definition of loss at the moment when it can no longer be evaded.
topics.reason: The accusative temporal adverb closes the loss definition and is specified by the following construct complement; 1:4 and 82:19 support judgment-day pressure.

words.gloss_range: the Resurrection or Standing, narrowed here to the event-day of accountability
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, maintaining, and establishment; local noun names the Day when persons stand for account
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ}} ({{tr:al-qiyāmah}}) specifies the event-time as the Day of Standing. The root field makes accountability bodily and concrete: people stand for account (83:6), while the ayah will close with {{ar:مُّقِيمٍۢ}} ({{tr:muqīmin}}), turning the same standing field into punishment that remains established.

topics.headline: the Day of Standing answers with standing punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the q-w-m arc: standing for account later returns as punishment that remains standing.
topics.reason: The genitive construct complement specifies the event-day, and the root echo with the closing adjective is locally strong; 83:6 and 41:30 provide contrastive standing scenes.

words.gloss_range: alert particle commanding attention before the final assertion

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby lexical anchor used in the prose

words.prose: {{ar:أَلَآ}} ({{tr:alā}}) commands attention at the pivot into the final declaration. After the believers define the losers, the alert plus {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) lifts the discourse into a sealing proclamation about the wrongdoers and their abiding location.

topics.headline: alert particle lifts the closing clause into proclamation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final line as a public seal after the believers' definition, not simply another quoted sentence.
topics.reason: The alert particle precedes the final emphatic particle and pivots after the quote into a closure formula.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle governing the final nominal punishment clause
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) governs the final nominal clause and confirms its predicate. The first {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) defined real loss; this second emphasis gives the destination, placing the wrongdoer class inside punishment rather than leaving the verdict abstract.

topics.headline: second emphasis seals the destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah move from defining loss to confirming destination.
topics.reason: The particle governs the wrongdoer label and scopes the prepositional predicate; it mirrors the earlier emphatic definition.

words.gloss_range: wrongdoers, narrowed here to the definite agentive class placed in punishment
words.root_gloss_range: injustice, misplacement, deprivation, and darkness; local participle selects moral wrong while darkness resonates with the obscured glance
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ}} ({{tr:al-ẓālimīna}}) names the class before locating it in punishment. The active participle makes wrongdoing an agentive identity, and the root field of injustice and darkness lets the final label look back to the hidden edge-glance: their obscured perception belongs to a larger moral disorder. References to self-wronging (2:57) and great wrong (31:13) ground the label without narrowing it to one subgroup.

topics.headline: the final class label gives moral cause for punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that punishment answers morally disordered action, not bad luck or mere exposure.
topics.reason: The definite active participle is the ism of the final emphatic particle; the base text keeps a general class while plus-reading pressure is only apparatus. References 2:57 and 31:13 support self-wronging and great wrong.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking containment as the predicate of the final clause
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) is the hinge of the final containment verdict. As the predicate phrase, it places the wrongdoers inside punishment as an enclosing state or environment, and the following adjective will make that environment stable rather than momentary.

topics.headline: the prepositional predicate makes punishment a location-state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands punishment as the environment they are in, not merely a penalty handed to them.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase functions as the predicate under the emphatic particle and keeps spatial and state containment active.

words.gloss_range: punishment or torment, narrowed here to an indefinite enclosing state of penal suffering
words.root_gloss_range: penal torment with a classical sweetness/freshness side outside the local selection; local Quranic usage selects punishment
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابٍۢ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābin}}) is the container-state named by {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}). Its indefiniteness classifies and magnifies without exhausting the measure, while the maṣdar-like noun lets punishment become a condition one is in; the sweetness side of the root is not selected locally, which sharpens the reversal into torment. Formulaic parallels include great punishment (2:7) and abiding punishment (5:37), but this clause lands on duration.

topics.headline: punishment becomes the enclosing state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final consequence as a punishment-condition whose measure is not exhausted by naming it.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the containment preposition and modified by the abiding adjective; references 2:7 and 5:37 show formulaic punishment severity and duration while the local emphasis falls on permanence.

words.gloss_range: abiding, established, or remaining, narrowed here to permanence as a property of punishment
words.root_gloss_range: standing, maintaining, abiding, and establishment; local active participle makes punishment durably established

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: Day of Standing as judgment time

words.prose: {{ar:مُّقِيمٍۢ}} ({{tr:muqīmin}}) is the ayah's closing landing. By agreeing with {{ar:عَذَابٍۢ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābin}}), it makes permanence a quality of the punishment itself; the q-w-m field turns duration into established presence, answering {{ar:ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ}} ({{tr:al-qiyāmah}}) with a punishment that stands and remains after exposure, definition, and proclamation.

topics.headline: the final adjective makes punishment stand and remain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah close not on pain alone but on punishment that stands and does not collapse.
topics.reason: The active participle agrees with the punishment noun in genitive indefiniteness and returns the q-w-m field from the Day of Standing; 5:37 supplies the recurring abiding-punishment formula.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: تَرَىٰهُمْ يُعْرَضُونَ ... يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِىٍّ
baseline_models.mechanism: Open display and concealed looking form an asymmetric field of vision: the addressee sees the people as exposed objects while their own gaze is lowered, marginal, and partly hidden.

activation_trace.role: Eye or insight perception gives the external observer an unimpeded view of the people.
Bringing something out for inspection makes the people the displayed objects of the scene.
Lowered head, gaze, voice, and limbs give the display its contracted bodily posture.
Breaking under coercive humiliation explains why the posture is compelled rather than chosen gentleness.
Directed ocular attention preserves an active attempt to see inside an otherwise passive display.
The eye, blink, or curtailed glance reduces that attempt to the smallest visual motion.
Concealment qualifies the glance, not the displayed bodies, sharpening the unequal visibility.

changed_reading.before: A scene in which humiliated people happen to look timidly at punishment.
changed_reading.after: A regime of unequal visibility in which they are fully inspectable but can exercise sight only through a contracted, concealed edge-glance.

baseline_models.mechanism: The noun-verb repetition turns loss into both identity and action, while its direct objects make the lost capital the person's own self and network of intimate belonging.

activation_trace.role: General diminution makes loss a reduction of the losers themselves, reinforced by the repeated root.
Commercial loss supplies a balance-sheet image in which the exposed stake is not external property.
The thing's very self or essence identifies the first lost asset with the agent's own whole identity.
The group formed by household, kinship, residence, or affiliation expands loss into relational belonging.

changed_reading.before: The wrongdoers lose a favorable outcome and are separated from family.
changed_reading.after: Loss has consumed both poles that could still count as theirs: the self that possesses and the intimate community through which that self belongs.

baseline_models.mechanism: Two forms of q-w-m bind the event of creatures rising to a punishment that stands, stays, or becomes their settled condition; the day does not merely begin pain but installs it.

activation_trace.role: Resurrection and the rising of creatures supply the initiating event in the repeated root.
Residence in a place or time gives muqim the settled persistence produced by that event.
Severe painful punishment names what the repeated q-w-m forms establish and sustain.

changed_reading.before: Punishment occurs on resurrection day and lasts.
changed_reading.after: The rising itself inaugurates a standing, settled condition: resurrection and duration are coupled through one root.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated address 'you see' first shows wrongdoers fearing what they earned as it falls and fixes upon them, then shows them seeing the punishment, and finally shows them as the objects displayed to it. The seers become the exhibit.

activation_trace.role: The first open act of seeing begins the staged visual recurrence with wrongdoers as its object.
Seeking and obtaining gain supplies the action whose result the wrongdoers now fear.
Falling and becoming fixed turns the earned result from an abstraction into something arriving upon them.
Seeing occurs both in the observer formula and in the wrongdoers' direct encounter, advancing the visual sequence.
Exposure for inspection completes the shift from seeing an outcome to seeing the agents displayed to it.
Their residual directed gaze keeps them conscious participants even after they become displayed objects.
The curtailed eye-glance marks the final collapse of the direct seeing present one ayah earlier.

structural_cues: 42:22, 42:44, and 42:45 repeat the second-person seeing formula while moving from feared earnings, to seeing punishment, to the people themselves being displayed.
The shift from رَأَوُا۟ in 42:44 to يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِىٍّ in 42:45 contracts their visual agency.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated seeing constructions, earned consequence, falling-upon, direct encounter, and passive display; I supply the directional arrow that reads them as successive stages. A live alternative is emphatic recurrence without a narrated chronology.

changed_reading.before: The focus is an isolated tableau of fearful looking.
changed_reading.after: It is the terminal visual stage of earned consequence: what they once saw approaching now fixes upon them, and those who looked become exposed objects able only to steal a glance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent active أَعْرَضُوا۟ and passive يُعْرَضُونَ reverse agency within one root: turning one's side away from the message is answered by being brought out and made to face what was evaded.

activation_trace.role: Turning away while presenting one's side supplies the active posture of evasion.
Being brought out for inspection reverses that posture into involuntary exposure.

structural_cues: The post-focus conditional فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُوا۟ stands within three ayat of the focus passive يُعْرَضُونَ and uses the same root with opposed voice and agency.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the active turning-away branch and passive display branch; I infer an ironic causal reversal from their adjacency. The alternative is a non-causal lexical echo joining warning and judgment.

changed_reading.before: They are simply presented to punishment.
changed_reading.after: Their exposure is a reversal of evasion: those who exercised agency by turning aside lose control of their side and are themselves turned into the presented object.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the surah q-w-m names voluntary establishment of religion and prayer and straight adherence to the commanded path. In the focus, the same root names resurrection and abiding punishment, converting refused self-establishment into imposed standing and emplacement.

activation_trace.role: Rising with resolve to an affair gives أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلدِّينَ the surah's first voluntary q-w-m demand.
Straightness and rectitude make the commanded stance directional and ethical.
Undertaking and establishing prayer repeats q-w-m as chosen practice.
The straight path closes the surah with the offered direction of q-w-m.
Resurrection makes standing universal and no longer voluntary.
Settled residence turns the imposed standing into an enduring condition.

structural_cues: أَقِيمُوا۟, ٱسْتَقِمْ, أَقَامُوا۟, ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ, مُّقِيمٍ, and مُّسْتَقِيمٍ distribute one root across command, practice, judgment, duration, and path.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the q-w-m recurrence and its branches of resolve, rectitude, resurrection, and residence; I infer a reversal from voluntary alignment to compulsory standing. A live alternative is broad root cohesion without punitive conversion.

changed_reading.before: Resurrection and abiding are conventional time markers around punishment.
changed_reading.after: The focus is the involuntary endpoint of the surah's standing vocabulary: one may establish and stand straight now, or be raised into a condition that remains established over oneself.

context_deltas.mechanism: Cultivation, earning, and increase build an acquisition economy; earned results then fall upon agents and can wreck and trap their vessels. The focus's repeated kh-s-r becomes the final account in which self and household, not merely profit, are the capital lost.

activation_trace.role: Gathering, earning, and labor make both harvest choices sustained projects of acquisition.
Seeking and obtaining gain names the wrongdoers' own productive action.
The acquired result falls and settles back upon its acquirers.
A second attribution to earnings carries the acquisition logic into the ship image.
Falling into destruction turns accumulated gain into the cause of catastrophic loss.
Trading loss supplies the final accounting category that answers the surah's repeated acquisition.
The self or very essence is revealed as part of the capital exposed to loss.
Household and intimate affiliation complete the account beyond the isolated individual.

structural_cues: 42:20 contrasts two harvest projects; 42:22 and 42:30 attach outcomes to what agents earned; 42:34 can wreck the ships by what their occupants earned.
The focus repeats kh-s-r first as an identity and then as a verb before naming its two direct objects.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies cultivation, acquisition, increase, falling consequence, earned wreck, and trading-loss branches; I supply the accounting arrow that treats these as one settlement process. The alternative is a looser sequence of moral cause and effect without economic integration.

changed_reading.before: The losers fail to gain salvation.
changed_reading.after: The surah's acquisition cycle closes with a negative settlement: what agents cultivated and earned returns upon them until the apparent owner and the owner's household are disclosed as the lost principal.

context_deltas.mechanism: Pairing, progeny, kin-affection, gift, alliance, and refuge make household a created network of mutual shelter. Immediately after the focus, protecting allies and refuge disappear; losing ahl therefore includes collapse of the relations by which a self is paired, continued, loved, and sheltered.

activation_trace.role: A counterpart joined to its counterpart supplies the basic relational architecture of household.
Progeny and descendants extend pairing into generational continuity.
Affection supplies the inward social bond rather than mere biological adjacency.
Kinship by womb and descent makes that affection specifically relational and familial.
Love, support, and alliance name the protective relation explicitly absent after the focus.
Taking shelter in a refuge supplies the protective function that is denied.
The distant spouse branch lets the denied refuge resonate, cautiously, with the lost domestic bond.
Gift without exchange frames children and family formation as bestowed rather than possessed capital.
Making one thing a partner to another closes the surah with constituted pairing.
The self as one's very identity is the node whose relational constitution collapses.
Household, kin, residence, and affiliation gather the distributed context relations into the focus anchor.

structural_cues: 42:11 and 42:49-50 bracket the surah with pairing and procreation, while 42:46-47 immediately follow the focus with no protecting allies and no refuge.
The coordinated objects أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ prevent household loss from being detached from loss of self.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies pairing, descent, kin-affection, gift, support, refuge, self, and household; I infer that these distributed relations form one sheltering network. The spouse branch of l-j-ʾ is especially distant, and the live alternative is simply literal loss of family members.

changed_reading.before: Each person loses self and separately loses family members.
changed_reading.after: The loss is relational unmaking: the self loses the paired, generative, affectionate, protective shelter through which it had household identity, and the next ayat confirm that no substitute alliance or refuge remains.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate legal-social sequence limits response to equivalence, leaves pardon and reconciliation open, exempts the vindicated victim, and places the path of liability only upon those who wrong people and exceed right. The focus label 'wrongdoers' therefore arrives after calibrated alternatives have been distinguished.

activation_trace.role: Answering an act with its consequence supplies the sequence's redress frame.
Equivalence limits redress to a matching response rather than uncontrolled retaliation.
Foregoing punishment and effacing fault keeps a non-punitive exit live.
Removing estrangement between people makes pardon reparative rather than passive.
Crossing the limit through aggression identifies the conduct that activates liability.
A right belonging to its holder supplies the boundary violated by aggression.
The traversable path becomes the construction's channel of warranted claim against the aggressor.
Withholding or blocking right specifies wrongdoing as an injury to people, not a free-floating label.
The focus designation carries the just-developed rights violation into the enduring consequence.
Painful punishment is placed after, and functionally constrained by, the calibrated redress corridor.

structural_cues: 42:40-43 distinguish equivalent response, pardon with reconciliation, justified self-vindication, aggression against people, patience, and forgiveness immediately before 42:44-45.
إِنَّمَا ٱلسَّبِيلُ عَلَى in 42:42 restricts the route of liability before 42:45 declares the wrongdoers in enduring punishment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies equivalence, pardon, reconciliation, vindication, aggression, right, restricted liability, and the repeated z-l-m label; I infer that this corridor controls how the focus punishment is read. The alternative is that the ethical sequence and judgment scene are adjacent but not juridically integrated.

changed_reading.before: The wrongdoers receive an undifferentiated punitive fate.
changed_reading.after: Their enduring punishment closes a carefully delimited social process: measured redress and reconciliation were available, victims were exempted, and liability attaches to those who crossed limits and withheld people's right.

context_deltas.mechanism: Return, path, protecting alliance, and refuge are successively denied around the focus. The prepositions of being displayed upon it and being in abiding punishment thus become a terminal spatial grammar: emplacement with no route back, out, or under protection.

activation_trace.role: Return to a former place supplies the escape the wrongdoers ask whether any path can reach.
A traversable extended road materializes the requested means of return.
Supportive alliance is denied as an interpersonal route out of the condition.
The repeated road is now explicitly absent rather than merely sought.
The day itself has no return, closing temporal reversal as well as spatial escape.
Refuge as a place of protective recourse closes the final alternative destination.
Passive placement before an object gives the terminal route pattern a bodily endpoint.
Residence in a place or time changes 'abiding' from bare duration into no-exit emplacement.

structural_cues: 42:44 asks for a return-path; 42:46 denies both allies and any path; 42:47 denies return, refuge, and effective repudiation.
The focus locates the people عَلَيْهَا and the wrongdoers فِى عَذَابٍ مُّقِيمٍ between those route denials.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated return, road, alliance, refuge, display, and residence images; I infer that their denials spatialize muqim as terminal emplacement. The alternative is that muqim marks duration only and the route language independently marks helplessness.

changed_reading.before: Abiding punishment means punishment that lasts a long time.
changed_reading.after: It is a settled no-exit location: they are placed before it after return is sought, and every road, protector, refuge, and temporal reversal is then closed.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The ship-to-person transfer is cross-domain and therefore surprising, but it remains anchored in focus q-w-m's branch of arrested standing and in passive display, while 42:32-34 explicitly move from running vessels to stillness, fixation, earned wreck, and inescapable entrapment. Downstream prose should present it as a material analogy for muqim, not identify the people with ships.

activation_trace.role: Free running and flowing establish the prior mobility from which arrest can be felt.
Loss of movement removes the propulsive condition of the vessels.
Fixity after motion gives the arrested vessels a stable exposed posture.
Entrapment from which one cannot disengage turns stillness into terminal capture.
Water becoming still or a mount stopping from exhaustion lets muqim carry an arrested-motion resonance.
Exposure for inspection gives the arrested condition its public, bodily form.

changed_reading.before: Muqim says only that punishment persists through time.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it also feels like arrested motion: once-running agents are stranded in an exposed, fixed condition from which earned consequence leaves no release.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation depends on the packet's non-dominant r-w-y mapping for QAC ر ء ي and on water/thirst branches of ع ذ ب, so it is deliberately form-distant; it remains packet-anchored through those exact focus inventories and through the surah's rain, revival, provision, and mercy sequence. Downstream prose must call it a material resonance and must not claim that تَرَىٰ literally means drinking or quenching.

activation_trace.role: The split inventory's quenching versus thirst image supplies a latent water state beneath the overt seeing form.
Refusal or inability to eat and drink under severe thirst makes punishment bodily deprivation.
Withholding and weaning from a thing make that deprivation sustained rather than momentary.
Rain construed as apportioned provision joins water to the surah's economy of bestowed sustenance.
Life-giving rain supplies the quenching material offered after despair.
Rain reviving dry herbage gives mercy a visible transition from desiccation to life.
Tender mercy identifies what the rain image distributes rather than merely depicting weather.

changed_reading.before: The visual clause and enduring punishment have no material relation to the surah's rain imagery.
changed_reading.after: As a contained split-root resonance, the exposed people inhabit permanent unquenching: rain elsewhere revives despairing dryness as mercy, while their punishment is figured as continued withholding from that life-giving provision.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The model crosses from revelation mechanics to bodily optics, which makes it surprising; it remains anchored in the focus roots of seeing and concealment and in context branches where hidden communication becomes light through a veil. Downstream prose should frame it as a contrastive architecture of disclosure, not equate the concealed glance with revelation.

activation_trace.role: Knowledge cast in hiddenness opens the surah with concealment that successfully communicates.
The repeated hidden transmission restates concealment as a medium of disclosure near the close.
A screening barrier makes mediated access possible without direct exposure.
Illumination names the disclosed result of the surah's hidden communication.
Open perception places the displayed people in full view.
Their own directed sight is still active but radically narrowed.
Concealment now belongs to an impaired glance rather than to a fruitful medium of knowledge.

changed_reading.before: The hidden glance is solely a bodily symptom of fear.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it inverts the surah's disclosure pattern: hidden communication can open into guiding light, but these fully exposed people retain hiddenness only as a constriction of their own sight.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: Moving from communal deliberation to judgment display is a cross-domain social reading, but the sh-w-r inventory itself supplies showing and drawing out opinion, while the focus supplies passive display and transfers effective speech to the believers. Downstream prose should qualify this as a structural contrast in agency, not a direct lexical derivation between shura and punishment.

activation_trace.role: Bringing something forth and displaying it makes communal affairs voluntarily presentable.
Drawing out judgment through reciprocal review gives that presentation a participatory voice.
Passive exposure changes voluntary presentation of an affair into involuntary presentation of persons.
Articulated speech belongs to the believers, marking who retains public interpretive agency in the scene.
The displayed people's contribution is reduced from deliberative speech to constrained looking.

changed_reading.before: The focus distributes roles only between punished people and commenting believers.
changed_reading.after: As a contained social contrast, the surah moves from persons who voluntarily display affairs and draw out one another's judgment to persons involuntarily displayed while public speech passes to another community.

strongest_changes: The adjacent ع ر ض forms reverse active turning-away into passive exposure.
The surah's voluntary q-w-m commands become involuntary resurrection and settled punishment.
Cultivation and earnings culminate in kh-s-r whose lost capital is self and household.
Repeated return, path, ally, and refuge denials spatialize muqim as no-exit emplacement.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah reconstruction exposed several mechanisms that a local reading could miss: a staged reversal from seeing to being seen, a root-level conversion of ethical standing into imposed standing, family as sheltering relation, and material outliers from arrested ships and the packet's r-w-y water split.
remaining_uncertainties: The active/passive and q-w-m recurrences are strong, but their causal direction remains a reader inference rather than explicit syntax.
The relational-shelter model integrates distant ayat and the spouse branch of l-j-ʾ, so its network reading should remain below the direct household sense.
The water, hiddenness, and ship activations are valid packet-anchored resonances but should not displace the focus ayah's ordinary visual and punitive constructions.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Those who turned aside are presented side-on and can look only from a concealed edge.** Lexical evidence: ع ر ض `B002` (presenting to view) and `B005` (turning one's side away), خ ش ع `B001` (low submission), ذ ل ل `B001` (abasement), ط ر ف `B001` (edge) and `B002` (glance), and خ ف ي `B001` (hiddenness). Structural cue and role: passive presentation exposes them, yet their own looking is reduced to a faint marginal glance. Abductive move: I infer a reversal: prior side-turning from address becomes forced side-position before consequence. Reading change: humiliation is expressed as loss of full visual and bodily orientation.

2. **Loss reaches both the living self and its network of belonging.** Lexical evidence: خ س ر `B001` (deficiency) and `B002` (trade loss), ن ف س `B011` (living soul-self), ء ه ل `B001` (people bound by belonging), ق و م `B013` (resurrection) and `B006` (station), plus ع ذ ب `B005` (punishment). Structural cue and role: duplicated loss takes self and family as objects, while **مُّقِيم** makes punishment a standing condition. Abductive move: I infer that the failed transaction liquidates both personal integrity and relational capital. Reading change: eschatological loss is social as well as individual.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 42:48 returns to **أَعْرَضُوا۟**, turning side-away from the messenger. The repetition confirms the retrospective reversal: voluntary side-turning becomes involuntary sideward exposure and a hidden edge-glance.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Open exposure compresses their visual agency into a hidden edge-glance.** **Lexical evidence:** ع ر ض `B002` (presenting a thing to view), خ ش ع `B001` (low humble submission), ط ر ف `B002` (blink or glance) with `B001` (edge), and خ ف ي `B001` (hiddenness), anchored in يُعْرَضُونَ ... يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِىٍّ. **Structural cue:** the ayah begins with the observer's unrestricted تَرَىٰهُمْ but gives the exposed people only an oblique concealed look; 42:44 had made their sight belated. **Assigned role:** presentation makes them fully visible, while edge and hiddenness reduce their own access to seeing. **Abductive move:** I infer a reversal of visual power from the opposed sight-lines. **Reading change:** humiliation is enacted as asymmetrical visibility, not only described as an inward feeling.
2. **Loss is relational depletion, not only individual defeat.** **Lexical evidence:** خ س ر `B001` (general deficiency), ن ف س `B012` (the very self), and ء ه ل `B001` (people bound by closeness and belonging), anchored in خَسِرُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ. **Structural cue:** 42:40 framed recompense; 42:49-50 will frame daughters, sons, pairing, and sterility as gifts and created states. **Assigned role:** loss removes both personal integrity and the network of belonging that constituted household life. **Abductive move:** I infer relational capital from the paired direct objects and the later gift-distribution. **Reading change:** final loss is collapse of self-in-relation, not a solitary negative balance.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 42:49-50 made loss of family newly concrete by presenting daughters, sons, mixed offspring, and sterility as configured gifts. The retrospective contrast turns خسران into loss of a gifted relational field, not merely loss of possessions.

baseline.text: Onların aşağılanmış halde ona sunulduklarını ve göz ucuyla gizlice baktıklarını görürsün. İnananlar şöyle der: Asıl kaybedenler, diriliş gününde kendilerini ve ailelerini kaybedenlerdir. Dikkat edin, haksızlık edenler kalıcı bir azap içindedir.

findings.text: Tamamen görünür biçimde sunulmaları ile yalnızca gizli bir kenar bakışı atabilmeleri arasındaki karşıtlık, aşağılanmayı görsel yetkinin kaybı olarak kurar.
Kayıp yalnızca bireysel yenilgi değildir; kişinin kendi canlı bütünlüğüyle yakınlık ve aidiyet ağının birlikte tükenmesidir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Judgment forces hidden loss into view while constraining the condemned to partial, lowered, or furtive sight.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Visibility is anatomized through posture and eye mechanics: bowing, subjugation, blinking, tear-struck sight, and edge-of-eye observation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Forced Display and Abasement
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: The condemned are placed on display, their bodies lowered as they are made mutually visible.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: display for inspection `quranic:root_001001:B002/m01`; bowed or downcast posture `quranic:root_000412:B001/m01`; broken subjugation `quranic:root_000519:B001/m01`; parties facing and seeing one another `quranic:root_000531:B004/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Exposure is imposed bodily. Those displayed cannot control the scene: humiliation lowers their posture even as concealment is removed and mutual visibility is forced upon them.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görmeyi hem gözle algılama hem de gözün işlevine benzetilen içsel kavrayış olarak kuruyor. Doğrudan göz tanıklığı bu çekirdeğin duyusal gerçekleşimidir; zihinsel görüş, uyku düşü ve başkalarına görünme amacı bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği görsel ya da içsel algıdır; belirli söz öbekleri ve bakma çabası ayrı kullanımlar olarak tutulur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın görme çekirdeği ile doğrudan göz tanıklığını ve görmeye çalışma bildiren bağlı kullanımlar birbirine karıştırılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi gözle ya da göz işlevi gören içsel kavrayışla algılamaktır. Gözün eriştiği yerde doğrudan görme, bu anlamın duyusal ve tanıklığa dayalı gerçekleşimidir.

facets.statement: Görülebilir bir şeyi gözle veya benzer bir içsel kavrayışla algılama.
Bir şeyi gözün eriştiği yerde doğrudan ve tanık olarak görme.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, gözle görmeyi temel alır ve bazı anlatımlarda bu algıyı içsel kavrayışa kadar genişletir; doğrudan göz tanıklığı özellikle belirtilir.
